WORKING RULES LEARNED: before I say a fix is possible, run the existing check that might already answer it; a reproduction must say WHICH copy of the script ran (a call through this repository executor runs the source tree); a pre-fix statement in a spec must be checked by running the full verb, not a help flag; write fails at the worktree base, not fails at a SHA; read the lane own self-review state first on a landing; compare read-class shell totals from the store with the disclosed kinds; do not redirect a command output to dev null, and verify an update-field write by reading the view, because the script exits 0 on an error; do not repeat a CLAUDE.md claim about the repository as a fact before reading the code it describes; read the epic Watches before analysing a defect, because the trigger of the routed-build failure was already recorded there and I re-derived it; before replacing an anchor, read the current value first and edit it, never write a shorter one from memory (the 2026-11-07 condensation replaced only the per-plan analysis paragraphs that landings and epic.md already carry); when a lane reports a host-load figure, check the daemon journal for its worktree to see whether its builds were routed, because in-process builds bypass the slot cap (and a removed worktree journal is empty, so read a lane journal while its worktree exists); a lane statement of no surface drift is checked against landing-check surface_delta, never accepted (landing-check takes --declared-paths and --realized-paths; without them the delta is unmeasured); the OpenCode session store keys a lane sessions to the MAIN checkout directory, not its worktree, so find the root session by its title, take its children by parent_id, and read tool calls from the assistant messages content items of type tool (names shell, edit, write, read, grep, question, subagent) in session_message, not from session_part; a leaf report is a lead: re-read every point it marks checked at its file:line before it is written into a landing, and mention the points not re-read; the ledger worktree has uncommitted paths while a land is pending, so git refuses a rebase onto main: when it has no commits of its own a fast-forward merge onto origin/main is the same result, and when the other machine landed the ledger and the paths overlap (epic.md, the anchor, the view) stash the pending paths, fast-forward, pop, and regenerate the anchor and the view through the scripts; a gate read that shows a staged spec claiming a whole directory tree must be narrowed to the directories it needs before the overlap is judged; a merge commit that came through the merge queue is a squash with one parent, so read the parent with git and name it in the leaf prompt, never take the lane base for it; do not stamp a landing row before the analysis returns, even when the value is certain, and stamp all four result fields (status, pr, landing, plan_marshall_plan_id) in one pass; a gate read of a fix must also ask whether the fix reads provider data that GitHub rewrites after the fact (a commit field that follows the newest head); a leaf prompt carries a landing narrative claims one by one, never merged into a clause; a leaf can grade a finding above what the Done-when supports, so re-grade it against the spec text and say so in the landing; a bare name that stands for a test in a gate is a claim about identity: before a fix plan is scoped, ask what a same-named replacement does to it; a combined plan above the six-deliverable guard needs the operator word and a recorded split order; a spec that orders a reader and also orders a property that reader cannot give is a spec defect: check each ordered reader against each ordered guarantee before staging; one command per Bash call, with no env assignment or semicolon prefix, even for a read-only probe; a plan that edits shared build code must justify it against the spec limit in its landing, and the orchestrator checks the diff for shared files the spec did not declare; a weekly API rate limit can stop a leaf mid-run (it resets 10:00 Europe/Berlin), and a SendMessage to the stopped agent resumes it from saved work; a spec with no queue row is read by the corpus gate as indeterminate (row_not_joined) and it ALSO makes every other staged spec comparison indeterminate, so nothing is emittable until a row exists: when the operator says spec and not stage, tell them what emission then needs; a fix that touches a path another plan declares goes into that plan when the plan is held, and into a separate Maven-only or surface-only plan when it is not; corpus set-verdict takes --rescoped n/a, no or yes (not true or false), the claim ordinal counts EVERY top-level bullet under Claim Labels in file order including the Verify-first clauses (read claims_total from a deliberate out-of-range probe), a contradicted verdict blocks the prep-ready test unless the spec absorbed it and the stamp says rescoped yes, and parallel set-verdict calls on one spec all landed (verified by counting the verdict lines);
